# Authentication

Every callout is authorized by a `BoxTokenProvider`: the runtime mints and
caches an access token, attaches it as a bearer token, and refreshes once
on a `401`. Construct the entry-point client with the provider for your
flow:

```apex
Box client = new Box(new BoxHttpClient(provider));
```

## Developer Token

A short-lived token from the Box developer console — handy for scripts and
tests.

```apex
BoxTokenProvider provider = BoxAuth.developerToken('DEVELOPER_TOKEN');
```

## Client Credentials Grant (server auth, no key)

```apex
BoxTokenProvider provider = BoxAuth.clientCredentials(
    'CLIENT_ID', 'CLIENT_SECRET', 'enterprise', 'ENTERPRISE_ID');
```

## JWT (server auth with a signing key)

The private key never appears in Apex — it lives in a Salesforce
certificate and signs via `Crypto.signWithCertificate`.

```apex
BoxTokenProvider provider = BoxAuth.jwt(
    'CLIENT_ID', 'CLIENT_SECRET', 'enterprise', 'ENTERPRISE_ID',
    'PUBLIC_KEY_ID', 'certificate_name');
```

## OAuth 2.0 (authorization code) — not available on-platform

Interactive OAuth needs a browser redirect and callback, which server-side
Apex cannot perform. Use the Client Credentials Grant or JWT above for
server-to-server access instead.
